subsystems.name: Constant-current source
subsystems.role: delivers a fixed 1–2 mA no matter how skin impedance drifts during a session.

subsystems.name: Electrodes
subsystems.role: the skin interface; their area sets the current density that determines both effect and burn risk.
parts: head strap or frame holding position

subsystems.name: Montage and headset
subsystems.role: keeps the active and return electrodes over the intended cortical targets, usually the left and right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex for depression work.

subsystems.name: Monitoring and dose control
subsystems.role: detects bad contact before it causes a skin lesion.

subsystems.name: Companion software
subsystems.role: guides home use and records adherence.

buildSteps.title: Fix the dose
buildSteps.detail: Choose target current, electrode area and session length, then model how the field spreads through a head from MRI-derived anatomy so the current density at the skin stays low.

buildSteps.title: Design the current path
buildSteps.detail: A boost converter drives a controlled current through the body circuit; firmware samples the actual current many times a second and corrects it, and a hardware limit caps total charge regardless of software failure.

buildSteps.title: Build the electrodes
buildSteps.detail: Large-area pads are made so contact is even; a dry spot concentrates current and is the usual cause of redness or a small burn. Sponges must hold enough saline for the whole session.

buildSteps.title: Write the safety firmware
buildSteps.detail: Impedance is checked before and during stimulation; the current is ramped up and down over tens of seconds to avoid tingling and to make placebo-controlled trials possible; poor contact aborts the session.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and test
buildSteps.detail: Skin-contact parts need biocompatibility testing, and prescription devices go through medical electrical safety and electromagnetic-compatibility testing before they can be sold as treatment.

buildSteps.title: Prove it in sham-controlled trials
buildSteps.detail: Randomised trials compare active against convincingly shammed stimulation; effects are modest and vary between studies, so sample size and blinding quality matter more than in drug trials.

buildSteps.title: Clear and monitor
buildSteps.detail: Prescription devices obtain regulatory clearance for a named condition; consumer headsets are sold without a medical claim, which shifts responsibility for safe use onto the buyer.

prerequisites.tech: Understanding of cortical excitability and plasticity
prerequisites.why: the mechanism — a small shift in resting membrane potential plus lasting, NMDA-dependent changes — is established in principle, but which patients respond and why is not.
current distribution depends heavily on individual anatomy; generic montages average over real differences.
saline sponges and conductive pads are cheap, but they must stay wet and in even contact for the whole session.
blinding is hard because active stimulation produces sensations; if participants can tell, apparent effects shrink or vanish.
only a small number of prescribed devices have been cleared for depression, in some jurisdictions; most headsets are sold as wellness products.

pathway.milestone: consumer headsets sold widely and a few prescription devices cleared for depression
pathway.unlocks: real-world data, but also unsupervised use and occasional skin injuries.

pathway.milestone: personalised dosing from individual head models and better-tolerated montages
pathway.unlocks: more consistent effects across people instead of averages that hide non-responders.

pathway.milestone: larger, better-blinded trials in depression, stroke rehabilitation and motor learning
pathway.unlocks: clear evidence of which uses deserve a clinical claim.

pathway.milestone: supervised home treatment combined with behavioural or cognitive training
pathway.unlocks: a low-cost add-on to therapy, if the effect sizes hold up.
